body:
This could be a red herring. Currently, even if a script doesn't reference itself in any way (directly or cyclically), GDScript resource instances are never unloaded until the engine shuts down: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/77513.

Regardless of that, when looking into why scripts don't normally raise leaked instance errors, I found that the engine does attempt to clean up the script cache and cyclic references during shutdown (code below linked from version 4.7, but it's identical to 4.6):

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f6ab5db28b9d989a3ae710d57410a123cf0e4b23/modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp#L2228-L2269

I also found out that in the master branch (4.8 dev), the GDScript shutdown routine had a lot of things added:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/893cf5cbfe789ae67c9389708e1428141bb39b18/modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp#L2222-L2303

@buttonmonkey do you mind trying out the latest available 4.8 dev build to see if the recently added code has fixed the issue, at least to reduce log pollution? (since the "scripts never get unloaded until shutdown" thing hasn't changed)

If you're new to this, don't forget to back up your project, because opening it in a new version of godot can break the project files in older versions of godot.
Closing as invalid, the report is verbose and appears to not be human authored, if the report is cleaned up and concrete reproduction is provided it can be reopened
